endorsements.quote: Using an external test set from an independent study site to test the trained model (external validation) is the ideal standard.
Details on all the model training processes used should be provided such that other researchers could reproduce them.

The metrics used to measure model performance should be presented with statistical uncertainty (e.g., 95% CI) and compared between models using appropriate statistical tests that determine the statistical significance of the metric differences, thereby addressing the clinical problems that the current study is meant to address.
If a subgroup analysis was performed, the subgroups for which the AI model performed best and worst should be indicated.

Accordingly, the distribution of variables (including demographics and clinical parameters) in the training, validation, and test sets should be reported and statistically compared to show that the distributions are similar across sets.
Accordingly, the processes used to de-identify and protect personal information should be fully described.
To prevent bias, the test set needs to represent the target population.

unlisted_practices: Pre-register AI study design, data handling, model configurations, and parameter tuning procedures before accessing data to prevent p-hacking.
Share source code, training data, and study data publicly, with documented code, library versions, and repository access, or state reasons for restricted access.
Report AI-related errors, adverse events, and patient safety risks with occurrence rates, causes, impacts, detection, and mitigation.
Report investigator adherence or non-adherence to protocols for AI use in clinical practice.
Report the quantity of missing data across model input features.
Report sensitivity analyses of model robustness under different assumptions or initial conditions.
Use a unique device identifier or regulatory marker to identify the AI model version in clinical trials, and document version changes with rationale.
Describe how the AI model's results are intended to be interpreted to prevent misapplication in clinical settings.
Use a flow diagram to show participant and data inclusion and exclusion at each stage.
Use common data elements to standardize variable definitions and formats across studies.
Report the training curve and learning-curve metrics of investigators who collected data for AI development.

screen.reason: The paper presents comprehensive reporting guidelines and a checklist for researchers developing and using AI models in healthcare to improve transparency and reproducibility.
